title: Seneca natural-questions evidence chain with competing causal models
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. Seneca Naturales quaestiones II distinguishes observed thunder/lightning phenomena, material elements in clouds, escape/fracture conditions, and competing explanations. A finite evidence chain preserves phenomenon identity while switching causal model and confidence; a single-cause weather label is the rival.

source.source_span: II.1–12 programme and air; II.12 lightning/thunder distinction and moist/dry elements; later Book II discussion of competing explanations
source_facts: Seneca distinguishes lightning, thunderbolt and thunder by observable effect/timing.
The account separates moist and dry exhalations, cloud enclosure, escape, fracture and the sound of thunder.
The text preserves disagreement among explanations and sometimes argues from a shared phenomenon to different causal models rather than collapsing them into one observation.

duplicate_screen.checked: ideas search/duplicates Seneca thunder/causal explanation and route-check observation/cause; Hippocratic prognosis and Pliny observation cards excluded as different health/evidence mechanisms
duplicate_screen.difference: This card preserves competing causal hypotheses over one phenomenon and their scope, rather than a single observed sign, medical prognosis, or Pliny's attributed correction.

worked_examples: COMPARE(friction_model,internal_escape_model,evidence)->qualified rival explanations, not one fixed label
constructor.consequence: One observed event retains identity while the causal explanation and confidence branch differ; a model that swaps dry/moist material or fracture/gradual escape changes the predicted sound/force relation. A single-cause rival predicts every thunder-like observation has one fixed explanation.
constructor.smallest_test: Require two complete natural-history passages sharing an event type but explicitly contrasting causal models, with a preserved observation-to-explanation scope.
constructor.rival: All atmospheric terms are independent labels and the causal alternatives are decorative, so no evidence changes the output.
assumptions: The source's competing explanations are represented as alternatives, not modernized as true physics.
Phenomenon identity is distinct from causal model identity.
failure_modes: The surviving translation is editorial and technical terms may not preserve Greek scope.
The passage may be argumentative exposition, not a process record.
Without independently fixed evidence and model markers, the constructor can fit arbitrary explanations.

dependencies: Source-only natural-philosophy account; no target meteorological meaning is proposed.
access: Source-only; no target, reserve, image, experiment, route, ledger, decoder, or root file access.
